full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal J: This petition for leave to appeal by the writ-petitioner is from the judgment and order dated 12.8.98 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 6079 of 1997 discharging the Rule Nisi. 

 2. The Writ-Petitioner claimed that 84.09 acres of land of C.S. Plot No. 565 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 107 of Mouza Tejkunipara under Police Station Tejgaon at present Gulshan, District Dhaka was recorded in the names of Bhawal Raj Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and others. 3.41 acres out of 84.09 acres of land were settled with ten-ants in 1925 and the rest 30.68 acres of land remained with the Court of Wards Estate of Bhawal Raj. The Government acquired in L.A. Case No. 55/58-59 18.68 acres of land for D.I.T. (now RAJUK) for construction of Tejgaon Gulshan Road. The then D.I.T. took possession of the land on 27.6.60. No compensation was paid to the writ-petitioner. Out of the acquired 'area 13 acres of unutilized land was released in favour of one Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others by the D.I.T. contrary to the finding of the High Court Division in Second Appeal No. -685 of 1970 which upon hearing of leave petition was confirmed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition No. 84 of 1974 and possession was handed over to them on 2.4.84, There were many cases between the Bhawal Raj Estate and the said Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others in the Civil Co: is on the allegations that the said bdul Khaleque Munshi and others created false and fabricated documents relating to be land belonging to the Bhawal Raj Estate. The cases were settled at rest by the decision of the Appellate Division against the writ-petitioner and others. The writ-petitioner took the matter to the Ministry concerned and the Chairman of RAJUK was given the responsibility to consider the representation of the writ-petitioner in respect of 13 acres of unutilized land. While the matter was pending for decision by the Chairman of RAJUK a deed of release being No. 3092 dated 2.4.84 was executed by respondent No. 1 RAJUK in favour of Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others which the writ-petitioner challenged in the writ petition. The writ-petitioner also prayed for a direction to cancel the plan approved, if any, for construction of building over 13 acres of land and also for a direction for not approving any plan for construction of house over the said land. 

 4. Respondent No. 2 stated that Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others being owners in possession transferred 13 acres of land to M/S. Capital Property Limited which after obtaining a sanctioned plan from the RAJUK started construction thereon. The Appellate Division by judgment dated 9.3.98 came to the finding that the property belonged to Abdul Khaleque Munshi and others who subsequently transferred the same to respondent No. 2. The writ-petitioner's case was not accepted by any Courts and all the Courts below correctly decided the matter. 

 6. The High Court Division considered the decree passed in Title Suit No. 75 of 1967 and found that the question of receiving compensation money has been settled by the decree of the Civil Court against the petitioner. Under Section 101(1) of the Town Improvement Act, 1953 it is the absolute right of RAJUK to deal with the property acquired for them. The release in favour of the owners was rightly done. 

 7. Mr. Shahidul Alam Chowdhury could not advance any cogent argument against the findings of the High Court Division.
